title: Basal Cell Skin Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Basal Cell Skin Cancer (BCC). Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (full-body skin exam with dermoscopy, shave/punch/excisional biopsy, Area H/M/L risk stratification by location and size, clinical margin assessment, indolent vs aggressive histologic subtyping, high-risk clinical features) -> Risk Stratification (Low-Risk vs High-Risk vs Locally Advanced laBCC vs Metastatic mBCC) -> Low-Risk local therapy (standard 4 mm excision, curettage and electrodesiccation, topical 5-FU/imiquimod or PDT, RT for nonsurgical candidates) -> High-Risk margin-controlled surgery (Mohs micrographic surgery or CCPDMA excision, wider excision with frozen/permanent section, adjuvant or definitive RT) -> laBCC systemic therapy (first-line Hedgehog inhibitor vismodegib 150 mg PO daily or sonidegib 200 mg PO daily; second-line cemiplimab 350 mg IV q3w) -> mBCC systemic therapy (first-line vismodegib; second-line cemiplimab; palliative cisplatin-based chemotherapy consideration). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Basal Cell Skin Cancer Version 2.2026.

a.text: Area H (mask area of face including central face, eyelids, eyebrows, periorbital skin, nose, lips, chin, mandible, preauricular and postauricular skin, temples, ears, genitalia, hands, feet): high-risk at any size. Area M (cheeks, forehead, scalp, neck, pretibial): high-risk at 10 mm or larger. Area L (trunk and extremities excluding pretibial, hands, feet): high-risk at 20 mm or larger.

b.text: Aggressive histologic subtypes (infiltrative, micronodular, morpheaform, basosquamous, sclerosing) behave as high-risk disease regardless of size or location and require margin-controlled surgery; indolent subtypes (superficial, nodular) with well-defined borders and small size qualify for low-risk local options.

c.text: Standard excision of low-risk BCC uses 4 mm clinical margins with postoperative margin assessment; curettage and electrodesiccation is reserved for low-risk non-hair-bearing lesions outside Area H; topical 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod, and photodynamic therapy apply to superficial BCC in nonsurgical candidates with counseling on lower cure rates and need for follow-up.

d.text: Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (vismodegib 150 mg PO once daily per ERIVANCE/STEVIE; sonidegib 200 mg PO once daily per BOLT) are first-line systemic therapy for laBCC and mBCC; both are teratogenic, so pregnancy must be excluded with strict contraception during and after therapy, and patients must be monitored for muscle spasms, alopecia, and dysgeusia.

e.text: Cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 3 weeks (anti-PD-1, EMPOWER-BCC 1) is second-line systemic therapy for laBCC or mBCC after progression on or intolerance to a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor; cisplatin-based chemotherapy is a palliative multidisciplinary consideration for metastatic disease.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Basal Cell Skin Cancer: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before risk stratification. Confirm tissue diagnosis, map location against Area H/M/L size thresholds, assess margins and histology, and flag high-risk clinical features.
bullets: Complete full-body skin examination with dermoscopy, documenting lesion size in millimeters, anatomic location, borders, ulceration, and photography of the index lesion.
Biopsy of suspicious lesion: shave, punch, or excisional biopsy with pathology documenting BCC subtype, differentiation, and perineural involvement where present.

Risk stratification by location and size: Area H (mask area of face, genitalia, hands, feet) is high-risk at any size; Area M (cheeks, forehead, scalp, neck) is high-risk at 10 mm or larger; Area L (trunk and extremities) is high-risk at 20 mm or larger.
Clinical margin assessment: well-defined borders versus poorly defined borders, including assessment for subclinical extension and fixation to deeper structures.
Histologic subtype: indolent (superficial, nodular) versus aggressive (infiltrative, micronodular, morpheaform, basosquamous, sclerosing).
High-risk clinical features: immunosuppressed patient, site of prior radiation therapy, perineural involvement, or recurrent lesion after prior treatment.

options.label: Workup Complete - Proceed to Risk Stratification

nodes.name: Risk Stratification
nodes.title: Basal Cell Skin Cancer: Risk Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign the risk group from Area H/M/L location-size criteria, margin definition, histology, recurrence, and extent of invasion; risk group selects the local or systemic pathway.
nodes.path: Basal Cell Skin Cancer / Risk Stratification
bullets: Low-risk BCC: Area L smaller than 20 mm or Area M smaller than 10 mm, well-defined borders, primary lesion, non-aggressive histology, immunocompetent host, no prior radiation at the site.

High-risk BCC: Area H at any size, Area M 10 mm or larger, Area L 20 mm or larger, recurrent lesion, aggressive histology, poorly defined borders, perineural involvement, immunosuppression, or prior radiation at the site.
Locally advanced BCC (laBCC): extensive invasion into adjacent structures such that curative surgery or radiation therapy is not feasible or would cause unacceptable morbidity.
Metastatic BCC (mBCC): histologically confirmed nodal or distant organ metastases on clinical examination and cross-sectional imaging.

options.label: Low-Risk Basal Cell Carcinoma (Area L <20mm, Area M <10mm, well-defined, primary, non-aggressive histology)
High-Risk Basal Cell Carcinoma (Area H any size, Area M >=10mm, Area L >=20mm, recurrent, aggressive histology, or poorly defined)
Locally Advanced Basal Cell Carcinoma (laBCC: extensive invasion, not amenable to curative surgery or RT)
Metastatic Basal Cell Carcinoma (mBCC: nodal or distant organ metastases)

nodes.name: Low-Risk Treatment
nodes.title: Low-Risk BCC: Standard Excision, C&D, Topical Therapy, or RT
nodes.description: Definitive local therapy for low-risk BCC: margin-assessed excision, curettage and electrodesiccation for selected lesions, topical or PDT options for superficial disease in nonsurgical candidates, or radiation when surgery is contraindicated.
nodes.path: Basal Cell Skin Cancer / Low-Risk / Treatment
bullets: Standard surgical excision with 4 mm clinical margins and postoperative margin assessment; re-excise for positive margins.
Curettage and electrodesiccation (C&D) for low-risk superficial non-hair-bearing lesions outside Area H in appropriate candidates.

Topical therapy or photodynamic therapy (PDT) for superficial BCC in nonsurgical candidates: 5-fluorouracil 5% cream twice daily for 6-12 weeks, or imiquimod 5% cream 5 times per week for 6 weeks; counsel on lower cure rates and schedule close follow-up.
Radiation therapy (RT) as primary treatment when surgery is contraindicated or declined; confirm suitability with radiation oncology.
Surveillance after definitive local therapy: full skin examination with dermoscopy at least annually, sun-protection counseling, and prompt biopsy of new or changing lesions.
nodes.regimenSummary: Standard 4mm Excision or C&D or Topical 5-FU/Imiquimod

nodes.name: High-Risk Treatment
nodes.title: High-Risk BCC: Mohs or CCPDMA Excision With RT Options
nodes.description: Margin-controlled surgery is preferred for high-risk BCC to conserve tissue and confirm complete removal; wider excision with section control and adjuvant or definitive radiation cover the remaining scenarios.
nodes.path: Basal Cell Skin Cancer / High-Risk / Treatment
bullets: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) preferred for tissue conservation and complete margin control, especially for Area H lesions and recurrent or aggressive-histology disease.
Surgical excision with complete circumferential peripheral and deep margin assessment (CCPDMA) as an alternative margin-controlled technique where Mohs expertise is unavailable.
Surgical excision with wider clinical margins (at least 4-6 mm) plus intraoperative frozen section or permanent-section margin analysis when Mohs or CCPDMA cannot be performed.
Adjuvant radiation therapy (RT) when margins are positive and re-excision is not feasible; definitive primary RT for nonsurgical candidates after multidisciplinary evaluation.
Surveillance after definitive therapy: skin and regional examination every 6-12 months for 2 years then annually, with a low threshold for re-biopsy of the treatment field.
nodes.regimenSummary: Mohs Micrographic Surgery (MMS) or CCPDMA Excision

nodes.name: Locally Advanced Treatment
nodes.title: laBCC: Hedgehog Inhibitor Then Cemiplimab
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for locally advanced BCC is a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor; cemiplimab follows for progression on or intolerance to Hedgehog inhibition.
nodes.path: Basal Cell Skin Cancer / Locally Advanced / Systemic Therapy
bullets: First-line Hedgehog pathway inhibitor: vismodegib 150 mg PO once daily (ERIVANCE and STEVIE trials) or sonidegib 200 mg PO once daily (BOLT trial); continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

WARNING: Hedgehog pathway inhibitors are teratogenic. Exclude pregnancy before starting, require strict contraception during and after therapy per labeling, and counsel against blood donation during treatment.
Monitor on Hedgehog therapy for muscle spasms, alopecia, dysgeusia, weight loss, and fatigue; interrupt or discontinue for intolerable toxicity per labeling.
Second-line for progression on or intolerance to a Hedgehog inhibitor: cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 3 weeks (anti-PD-1, EMPOWER-BCC 1 trial) with immune-related adverse event monitoring.
Reassess surgical or RT candidacy at response; involve multidisciplinary dermatology, surgery, radiation oncology, and medical oncology throughout.
nodes.regimenSummary: Vismodegib 150 mg PO Daily (or Sonidegib 200 mg); 2L Cemiplimab 350 mg IV q3w

nodes.name: Metastatic Treatment
nodes.title: mBCC: Vismodegib Then Cemiplimab
nodes.description: First-line systemic therapy for metastatic BCC is Hedgehog inhibition with vismodegib; cemiplimab follows for progression or intolerance, with palliative chemotherapy as a multidisciplinary consideration.
nodes.path: Basal Cell Skin Cancer / Metastatic / Systemic Therapy
bullets: First-line Hedgehog inhibitor: vismodegib 150 mg PO once daily (ERIVANCE trial, confirmed objective responses in metastatic disease); continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
Apply the same teratogenicity precautions as in laBCC: exclude pregnancy, require strict contraception, and monitor for muscle spasms, alopecia, and dysgeusia.
Second-line for progression on or intolerance to Hedgehog inhibitor: cemiplimab 350 mg IV every 3 weeks (anti-PD-1, EMPOWER-BCC 1) with immune-related adverse event monitoring.
Multidisciplinary consideration of cisplatin-based chemotherapy for palliation in selected metastatic patients, particularly after checkpoint inhibitor progression.
Stage with cross-sectional imaging at baseline and every 8-12 weeks on systemic therapy; offer clinical trial enrollment at every line.
nodes.regimenSummary: Vismodegib 150 mg PO Daily -> Cemiplimab 350 mg IV q3w
